chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid and Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Shuʿayb, from Abū Baṣīr, and Faḍālah, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Muskān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān, all of them from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: that he was asked about a man who was in...

A cold land, and he feared that if he performed ghusl, hardship would befall him because of the ghusl—what should he do? He عليه السلام said: “He performs ghusl, even if whatever may befall him does befall him.”

He said, and mentioned: “Indeed, I was ill, in severe pain, and janābah befell me while I was in a cold place. It was a very windy and cold night, so I called the servant-boys and said to them: Carry me and wash me. They said: We fear for you. So I said to them: It is unavoidable. So they carried me, placed me upon pieces of wood, then poured water over me and washed me.”

key_terms.أَرْضٍ بَارِدَةٍ: a cold land or environment in which performing ghusl is difficult
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ghusl (ritual bath), here required due to janābah
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.عَنَتٌ: hardship, distress, or harm feared from performing ghusl
key_terms.لَيْسَ بُدٌّ: it is unavoidable or there is no alternative

ai.seo_question: What should a person in janābah do if performing ghusl in severe cold may cause hardship?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of ghusl in severe cold and hardship, presenting a case in which ghusl is still performed despite fear of difficulty. It also recounts a personal example of enduring illness and harsh weather while insisting on ritual purification from janābah.
